Implementation Plan

I've finished the investigation and the plan is below. The hole is real: the env-lookup loop in `render_prompt.sh` resolves any `{{NAME}}` in an untrusted reviewer or editor body against the environment.

## Summary

The issue is confirmed on the planning ref `ai/issue-9341` (HEAD `38bdce847f9a08eb91fc62ce1cffd313316c3207`; integration branch mismatch: false). In `scripts/render_prompt.sh`, `collect_prompt_placeholders` reads every `{{NAME}}` token from the file being rendered. The loop after it looks up each name in the environment with `${!placeholder_name}` and passes the value on as `--var NAME=<value>`. Three callers render bodies that already contain PR diff, comment and check-run text, with `RENDER_PROMPT_INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED=1 RENDER_PROMPT_SKIP_SYNTAX_VALIDATION=1` set:
- `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` line 3059 (the reviewer body)
- `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` line 3213 (the per-model overlay render)
- `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` line 1946 (the editor body)

The "Run reviewer models" step in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` sets `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}`. So a `{{GH_TOKEN}}` written in a PR diff or comment is replaced by the token value, which then goes to the model providers and also shows up in process argv.

`scripts/render_prompt.py` is not part of the problem. `collect_legacy_env_values()` reads only `WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION`, `SEMBLE_PREFETCH` and `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS`. `render_prompt_text` substitutes in one pass, so text that comes in as a value is never expanded again. The shell loop is the only place an arbitrary environment variable gets in.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/render_prompt.sh`
- `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`
- `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`
- `tests/test_render_prompt_env_placeholder_guard.py` (new)
- `changelog.d/9465-render-prompt-env-secret-guard.md` (new)

## Acceptance
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_env_placeholder_guard.py::test_untrusted_body_does_not_substitute_env_values red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_env_placeholder_guard.py::test_trusted_template_denies_credential_like_env_placeholders red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_env_placeholder_guard.py::test_untrusted_body_keeps_fixed_allowlist_substitution
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_env_placeholder_guard.py::test_review_render_subshells_unset_github_tokens red-on-base
ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py
ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: script-only hardening covered by the PR tests; no post-merge workflow is needed to confirm it.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/render_prompt.sh`

**a. Mark untrusted bodies.** Add a new flag variable `RENDER_PROMPT_BODY_IS_UNTRUSTED` (a grep found no existing use of the name), defaulting to `false`.
- Set it to `true` when either `RENDER_PROMPT_INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED` or `RENDER_PROMPT_SKIP_SYNTAX_VALIDATION` is truthy. Accept the same values the two existing `case` blocks accept (`1|true|yes|on|y`, any case), and set the flag inside those blocks.
- Base the flag only on those two env vars. Do not base it on `INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED_FLAG_ADDED`: the trusted `PROMPT_PRELUDE_REFACTOR_ENABLED` assembly path also adds `--input-already-assembled`, and that path must keep its env lookups.

**b. Add a credential-name denylist.** Add a new function `is_credential_like_placeholder_name` (name confirmed unused), defined next to `append_render_var` and keeping the file's tab and brace-on-new-line style. It upper-cases the name, then returns 0 (deny) when any of these is true:
- The name does not match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`. This blocks positional or special parameters such as `{{1}}`, which `${!1}` would otherwise resolve.
- The name contains `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `KEY`, `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD` or `CREDENTIAL`.
- The name starts with `GH_`, `GITHUB_` or `ACTIONS_`.
- The name has `PAT` as a whole underscore-separated segment: `PAT`, `PAT_*`, `*_PAT` or `*_PAT_*`. A segment match keeps names like `*_PATH` from being denied by mistake.

**c. Gate the env-lookup loop.** The loop is the `while IFS= read -r placeholder_name … done < <(collect_prompt_placeholders …)` block.
- When `RENDER_PROMPT_BODY_IS_UNTRUSTED=true`, skip the loop entirely. Only the four fixed `append_render_var` calls that already run before it apply (`WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION`, `SEMBLE_PREFETCH`, `SERENA_TOOL_HINTS`, `MODEL_FAMILY_OVERLAY`). Don't call `collect_prompt_placeholders` at all on this path, so names from untrusted text are never read.
- On the trusted path, call `is_credential_like_placeholder_name` before the `${!placeholder_name}` lookup. If the name is denied, `continue` without reading its value. When the variable is set, print one stderr line naming the placeholder but not its value, for example `render_prompt.sh: not substituting credential-like placeholder {{NAME}} from the environment`. The placeholder stays as literal text. If a contract lists that name as required, `validate_contract` then fails the render, which is the correct fail-closed result.
- Add a comment above the gate explaining the exfiltration path and pointing to this security finding.

**d. Keep everything else as it is:** placeholder collection from `PLACEHOLDER_SOURCE_FILE` (the trusted template, or the trusted assembled template), argument order, and the exec/exit behaviour.

### 2. `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`

In both render subshells (around line 3059 and around line 3213), add `unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN GH_PAT` right after the `cd`. Each is a `( cd …; … )` subshell, so this only affects the render process; the parent step's later `gh` calls still have the token. Add a one-line comment saying why.

### 3. `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`

Make the same `unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN GH_PAT` change inside the editor render subshell (around line 1946).

### 4. `tests/test_render_prompt_env_placeholder_guard.py` (new)

Follow the subprocess harness in `tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py`: `bash scripts/render_prompt.sh <file>`, `cwd=REPO_ROOT`, a minimal env with `PATH`/`HOME` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, a temp directory, and `timeout=60`. Tests:
- **`test_untrusted_body_does_not_substitute_env_values`**: a body containing `{{GH_TOKEN}}`, `{{OPENROUTER_API_KEY}}` and `{{CUSTOM_VAR}}`, with matching sentinel env values, rendered with both flags. Then the same body with each flag on its own. Expect exit 0, no sentinel in stdout, and the literal tokens kept.
- **`test_untrusted_body_keeps_fixed_allowlist_substitution`**: with the untrusted flags set, `{{MODEL_FAMILY_OVERLAY}}`, `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}`, `{{SEMBLE_PREFETCH}}` and `{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}` still render from env and `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS`.
- **`test_trusted_template_denies_credential_like_env_placeholders`**: a temp `mode-guardtest.txt` with no contract and no flags. Credential-like names are left literal and their sentinels never appear in stdout or stderr: `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_PAT`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `TG_BOT_SECRET`, `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, `MY_PAT`, and `1`. Non-credential names still render from env: `{{CUSTOM_PLACEHOLDER}}`, `{{BUILD_PATH}}`. Stderr names the denied placeholder.
- **`test_review_render_subshells_unset_github_tokens`**: a static check that each of the three render subshells in the two review scripts contains `unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN GH_PAT` before its `render_prompt.sh` call.

### 5. `changelog.d/9465-render-prompt-env-secret-guard.md` (new)

A `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` fragment in the same format as the existing fragments, describing the fix. Use a non-closing `Refs #<this issue>`.

## Data structures affected
None. No JSON or DB fields change, and no env var names are added or renamed. `RENDER_PROMPT_BODY_IS_UNTRUSTED` is a script-local shell variable, not an input.

## API or interface changes
- **`scripts/render_prompt.sh`, untrusted bodies.** When `RENDER_PROMPT_INPUT_ALREADY_ASSEMBLED` or `RENDER_PROMPT_SKIP_SYNTAX_VALIDATION` is truthy, only the four fixed placeholders are filled from env. Before, any `{{NAME}}` whose variable was set got filled. No caller in the repo depends on the old behaviour: the reviewer and editor heredocs use only `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` and `{{MODEL_FAMILY_OVERLAY}}`.
- **`scripts/render_prompt.sh`, all renders.** Credential-like names are never filled from env. No template under `prompts/` uses such a name; the only `{{KEY}}` in the repo is in a comment in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`.
- **Existing outputs.** stdout and exit codes stay the same for every current render. The new stderr line appears only when a denied name is used and its variable is set.

Data flow:
1. The review step env holds `GH_TOKEN`, and the body file holds untrusted text.
2. The render subshell runs `unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN GH_PAT`.
3. `render_prompt.sh` sees the untrusted flags, so it skips placeholder collection and adds only the four fixed `--var` values.
4. `render_prompt.py` substitutes those four in one pass and leaves every other `{{…}}` literal.

Failure modes:
- **A trusted template genuinely needs a credential-like name.** That placeholder renders literally, a stderr line names it, and a contract that requires it fails the render. Recovery: rename the placeholder to a non-credential name and pass the value explicitly.
- **A consumer's own caller relied on env lookups for an untrusted body.** Its custom placeholders now stay literal. Recovery: pass the value through one of the fixed variables, or render the trusted template first and append the untrusted text afterwards.

## Decisions

### D1 — Skip env lookups entirely for untrusted bodies
- **Chosen:** when either untrusted flag is set, never collect placeholder names from the body; pass only the four fixed variables.
- **Alternatives considered:** keep collecting but filter names through the denylist only; read names from `prompts/contracts/<mode>.yml`.
- **Why:** a d
